Plot the trend of a gene

Source: R/plotTrend.R
plotTrend.Rd

plotTrend() plots the pseudo-bulk counts of a gene along the binned pseudotime of each path, with the curves of its selected model (sc.t.fit()).

Usage

plotTrend(
  scmpObj,
  feature_id,
  xlab = "Pooled Pseudotime",
  ylab = "Pseudobulk Expression",
  smoothness = 0.01,
  logs = NULL,
  logType = "log",
  pseudoCount = 1,
  significant = TRUE,
  summary_mode = "median",
  curves = TRUE,
  lines = FALSE,
  points = TRUE
)

Arguments

scmpObj

A ScMaSigPro object.

feature_id

The name of a gene.

xlab

The label of the x axis.

ylab

The label of the y axis; with logged points it becomes, for example, log(ylab).

smoothness

The step of the pseudotime grid of the curves: the smaller, the smoother.

logs

Whether to log the points: the counts of the bins, divided, for log-link fits, by the size factors stored in the design. The fitted curve is the polynomial of the selected model on the scale of the link: the log of the mean under the log link, the mean itself under the identity link. The default, NULL, logs the points when the fits used the log link and draws them as they are otherwise, so that points and curve are on the same scale.

logType

The log of the points: "log", "log2" or "log10".

pseudoCount

The number added to the points before the log.

significant

Whether the gene must be in a gene list of sc.filter().

summary_mode

How the points of each binned pseudotime and path are summarised for the lines: "median" or "mean".

curves

Whether to draw the fitted curves.

lines

Whether to draw lines through the points.

points

Whether to draw the points.

Value

A ggplot object.

See also

Other plots: plotBinTile(), plotDiagnostics(), plotIntersect(), plotTrendCluster()

Author

Priyansh Srivastava spriyansh29@gmail.com

Examples

data("scmp.ob", package = "scMaSigPro")
plotTrend(scmp.ob, "Gene10")
